Explain the example for share a module

blocks.text: A module is a Sass file that shares values or recipes. @use loads it and gives its members a clear name prefix.
Use Dart Sass on your computer. Install Node.js first, with help if needed. Save SCSS examples as lesson.scss and run npx sass lesson.scss lesson.css. This site does not compile Sass.

blocks.title: Share a module

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `@use` loads a Sass module once. A module prefix keeps its variables and functions distinct from local names.

blocks.text: Save the two labelled sections as separate files. Building lesson.scss makes a navy h1 rule.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Keep @use at the start of the file. Do not paste both file sections into one file without splitting them.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Add a second colour to _colours.scss and use it.
